verification.reason: legacy manifests trusted; pass --verify-original to re-verify them; M03 audits are prior evidence with current source hashes checked

sources.reason: C compiler candidate; verify_matches.py reports 62 differing bytes (the same addresses are matched by matches_s08_2_x86.json)
C++ compiler comparison; semantic evidence, not an exact-match claim

crosscheck.scope: legacy match manifests only; audited M03 code is added separately

unit_definition: Code units are address bands of the indexed function spans (16 KiB bands within each code region), a stand-in for translation units until a unit map exists. Data units are image pieces from layout.json.

units.label: PE headers, Rich header, section table
.text file padding after its virtual end
Read-only data before the import directory
Read-only data after the import directory
.rdata file padding after its virtual end
.rsrc file padding after its virtual end

playable.next_blocker: S2010: scripted tick limit reached; further gameplay remains unverified.

caveats: Ported is a reviewed claim, not an x86 match: native code or a test covers the function, and the x86 match stays a separate, orthogonal track.

Tests-only is weaker evidence than oracle-verified (a test names the function, but no original-x86 oracle window proves it); adapter-tested covers Win32 or library behaviour replaced by a tested adapter. The three ported classes are reported separately.
Spans include tables, padding and thunks: a span runs from a function start to the next indexed start, and the Ghidra body size can be smaller.
Region seams are accurate to a few hundred bytes; a seam function is never decided by a rule.

Private receipts are not re-hashed at build time: the page shows only a receipt's name and sha256. Cited committed src/ and tests/ files are re-hashed, so changing one needs extract_function_evidence.py --write and build_function_ledger.py --write before this map can be rebuilt.
